### R66. Origin minimum of symmetric midpoint-convex functions and generation of S₄ by two permutations

- **Statement.** Every R : ℚ³ → ℚ that respects rational equality, is midpoint convex and is invariant under the three double sign flips satisfies R(0,0,0) ≤ R(x,y,z). In a 4-tuple model of S₄, the adjacent transpositions satisfy the braid relations; (1 2) and (0 2 1 3) do not commute, satisfy g₁² = id and g₂⁴ = id, and generate all 24 permutations.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`PromislowFracton.Palomar.t3a_v4_convex_ronkin_origin_minimum`](https://github.com/0thernes/promislow-fracton-amoeba/blob/c829ab811568a13e2283db2175f684e35b17c816/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L43), [`PromislowFracton.Palomar.t3c_artin_b4_and_full_s4_monodromy`](https://github.com/0thernes/promislow-fracton-amoeba/blob/c829ab811568a13e2283db2175f684e35b17c816/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L47), [`PromislowFracton.v4_convex_ronkin_origin_minimum`](https://github.com/0thernes/promislow-fracton-amoeba/blob/c829ab811568a13e2283db2175f684e35b17c816/lean/PromislowFracton/NonHermitianAmoeba.lean#L73), [`PromislowFracton.artin_b4_relations_and_s4_monodromy_generation`](https://github.com/0thernes/promislow-fracton-amoeba/blob/c829ab811568a13e2283db2175f684e35b17c816/lean/PromislowFracton/NonHermitianAmoeba.lean#L274); axioms: t3a: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; t3c: propext. Ronkin functions and the monodromy of Ψ(α̃) appear only in Rust/Python numerics.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** The minimum is not strict: the constant function satisfies all hypotheses.
- **Limit.** No Ronkin function or real-valued function is formalized.
- **Limit.** No braid group B₄ is defined, and that the two permutations are monodromies is numerical.

### R67. Integer octonion composition, Moufang identities, non-associativity, sedenion zero divisor, and 4D annihilator

- **Statement.** For the 8-dimensional algebra on Z^8 given by the stated Fano table: N(xy) = N(x)N(y) and the left, right and middle Moufang identities hold for all x, y, z; [e1, e2, e3] = -2 e6 != 0. In integer Cayley-Dickson sedenions, (e1+e10)(e3+e14) = 0, and ker(L_{e1+e10}) has a unique unimodular rank-4 Z-basis bijection (Z^4).
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`Octonionica.OctonionsSedenions.oct_degen_graves_eight_square`](https://github.com/0thernes/octonionica/blob/b485fd9f67451ce8e7abfd95be85199782684955/lean/OctonionicaProofs/OctonionsSedenions.lean#L31), [`Octonionica.OctonionsSedenions.oct_left_moufang`](https://github.com/0thernes/octonionica/blob/b485fd9f67451ce8e7abfd95be85199782684955/lean/OctonionicaProofs/OctonionsSedenions.lean#L313), [`Octonionica.OctonionsSedenions.oct_right_moufang`](https://github.com/0thernes/octonionica/blob/b485fd9f67451ce8e7abfd95be85199782684955/lean/OctonionicaProofs/OctonionsSedenions.lean#L334), [`Octonionica.OctonionsSedenions.oct_middle_moufang`](https://github.com/0thernes/octonionica/blob/b485fd9f67451ce8e7abfd95be85199782684955/lean/OctonionicaProofs/OctonionsSedenions.lean#L299), [`Octonionica.OctonionsSedenions.oct_strictly_non_associative`](https://github.com/0thernes/octonionica/blob/b485fd9f67451ce8e7abfd95be85199782684955/lean/OctonionicaProofs/OctonionsSedenions.lean#L52), [`Octonionica.OctonionsSedenions.sedenion_zero_divisor_collapse`](https://github.com/0thernes/octonionica/blob/b485fd9f67451ce8e7abfd95be85199782684955/lean/OctonionicaProofs/OctonionsSedenions.lean#L346), [`Octonionica.OctonionsSedenions.sedenion_infinite_zero_divisor_family`](https://github.com/0thernes/octonionica/blob/b485fd9f67451ce8e7abfd95be85199782684955/lean/OctonionicaProofs/OctonionsSedenions.lean#L356), [`Octonionica.OctonionsSedenions.sedenion_annihilator_iff_unique_basis4`](https://github.com/0thernes/octonionica/blob/b485fd9f67451ce8e7abfd95be85199782684955/lean/OctonionicaProofs/OctonionsSedenions.lean#L386); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
- **Audit (2026-11-27).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement matches the stated claim; prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** Proved over Z (integer coordinates) only; the extension to real octonions by the polynomial-identity argument is not formalized.
- **Limit.** Classical results (eight-square identity, Moufang 1935, Cayley-Dickson); an Isabelle AFP formalization of octonions (2018) already exists.
- **Limit.** In v1.3.0, sedenion_annihilator_iff_unique_basis4 upgrades the scalar-rescaling family to the exact unimodular rank-4 Z-module bijection ker(L_{e1+e10}) ~= Z^4 (wired into T1).

- **Limit.** Non-integrability of the octonionic almost complex structure on S^6 is classical (Eckmann-Frolicher and Ehresmann-Libermann 1951); the norm identity is Gray's constant-type condition. The existence of other complex structures on S^6 stays open and is not addressed.

### R69. 27D Albert Jordan algebra J3(O(Z)): universal Jordan identity, Freudenthal cubic, and Peirce primitivity

- **Statement.** For all Hermitian 3x3 matrices X, Y over O(Z) with X∘₂Y = XY+YX: X∘₂Y = Y∘₂X, X∘₂X# = 2det(X)I, X³ − 2Tr(X)X² + 4S(X)X − 4det(X)I = 0, and universally ((X∘₂X)∘₂Y)∘₂X = (X∘₂X)∘₂(Y∘₂X). For all u, v ∈ O(Z), P(u,v) has P# = 0, det P = 0, P∘₂P = 2Tr(P)P, and universal Peirce primitivity 2(P∘₂(P∘₂X)) − (P∘₂P)∘₂X = 2Tr(P∘₂X)P.

### R71. Ramanujan tau(1..20): Euler product equality, mod-691, full Hecke relations, and integer Deligne bounds

- **Statement.** Truncated at q^20, (E4^3 - E6^2)/1728 is integral and equals Ramanujan's Euler product q*prod_{m=1}^{20}(1-q^m)^24 identically (propext only); for 1 <= n <= 20, tau(n) != 0 and tau(n) = sigma_11(n) mod 691; all coprime Hecke multiplicativity relations mn <= 20, all prime-power recurrences (4, 8, 16, 9), and exact integer Deligne bounds tau(p)^2 <= 4 p^11 hold for all 8 primes p <= 19.

- **Statement.** For explicit 2x2 matrices F, R over Z[zeta_10]: F^2 = I, direct 3x3 matrix Mac Lane pentagon M2(F)M1(F) = R3(F)M1(F)M2(F) (0 axioms), both hexagons, and Artin B3 braid relation s1 s2 s1 = s2 s1 s2 hold. ### R73. Markov tree: reachability, coprimality, singular triples, mod 3/4, branches, binary forms, and Hurwitz sqrt(5)

- **Statement.** For positive integer solutions of x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 3xyz: Vieta descent reaches (1,1,1) universally; all triples are pairwise coprime; only (1,1,1) and (1,1,2) have repeated entries; 3 !| m and residues mod 4 are (1,1,1) or permutations of (2,1,1); Fibonacci and Pell branches hold; shared z divides (x1y2-x2y1)(x1y2+x2y1); k^2+1 = lz gives disc 9z^2-4; and |(2p-q)^2 - 5q^2| >= 4 for all (p,q) != (0,0).

- **Audit (2026-11-27).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement matches the stated claim; prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** The Markov uniqueness conjecture remains open; the divisor relation is a necessary condition that follows from x^2 + y^2 = 0 mod z and holds for identical or permuted triples, so it does not constrain counterexamples by itself.
- **Limit.** In v1.3.0, hurwitz_golden_norm_barrier proves the exact Hurwitz sqrt(5) barrier |(2p-q)^2 - 5q^2| >= 4 for all (p,q) != (0,0) (and markov_binary_form_discriminant proves disc = 9z^2 - 4); the general Lagrange spectrum beyond sqrt(5) remains unformalized.
- **Limit.** The Rust BFS over the 231 triples with maximum <= 10^15 is outside Lean and far below published verification ranges.
- **Limit.** Congruences and Hurwitz barrier are classical (Hurwitz 1891, Frobenius 1913).
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin (latest release `zenodo-2026-11-28`). They are not covered by this audit.

### R74. Jacobi symbol reciprocity laws and uniqueness of square roots of -1 modulo odd prime powers

- **Statement.** For odd n ≥ 1 the Jacobi symbol (built from Euler's criterion) satisfies the (−1/n) and (2/n) laws, multiplicativity, (a²/n) = 1 when gcd(a,n) = 1, and reciprocity for coprime odd m, n ≥ 1. For an odd prime p and k ≥ 1, if pᵏ divides r₁²+1 and r₂²+1 then pᵏ divides r₁−r₂ or r₁+r₂.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`ApollonianSandpileMarkov.Palomar.t1b_jacobi_reciprocity_master`](https://github.com/0thernes/apollonian-sandpile-markov/blob/94ece6a8dce9c9a30c6a2ada2eb335cb0501f770/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L23), [`ApollonianSandpileMarkov.Palomar.t3c_hensel_sqrt_neg1_prime_power_uniqueness`](https://github.com/0thernes/apollonian-sandpile-markov/blob/94ece6a8dce9c9a30c6a2ada2eb335cb0501f770/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L59); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Zero-Mathlib Lean 4.35.0 development.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement matches the stated claim; prior work: known mathematics.
- **Re-audit pending.** Audited at commit `94ece6a`; the archive pin has since moved to `bc6464b`.
- **Limit.** Classical results (Gauss, Jacobi, Eisenstein 1844 proof method); the contribution is a Mathlib-free formalization.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin (latest release `zenodo-2026-11-28`). They are not covered by this audit.

<a id="r75"></a>
### R75. Absence of square curvatures in three integral Apollonian circle packings

- **Statement.** In the Apollonian packings generated by (−3,5,8,8), (−7,17,12,20) and (−11,21,24,28) — every quadruple reachable from the root by the four Descartes reflections — no curvature equals m² for any integer m. Supporting identities: the reflections are involutions preserving the Descartes form, and (a+b)(a+c) = a² + k² for Descartes quadruples.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`ApollonianSandpileMarkov.Palomar.t1c_hkrs_apollonian_reciprocity_obstruction`](https://github.com/0thernes/apollonian-sandpile-markov/blob/94ece6a8dce9c9a30c6a2ada2eb335cb0501f770/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L26), [`ApollonianSandpileMarkov.Palomar.t1a_descartes_lorentzian_and_gaussian_norm`](https://github.com/0thernes/apollonian-sandpile-markov/blob/94ece6a8dce9c9a30c6a2ada2eb335cb0501f770/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L20); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Formalizes Haag-Kertzer-Rickards-Stange Theorem 1.6 and two Table A instances.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement matches the stated claim; prior work: known mathematics.
- **Re-audit pending.** Audited at commit `94ece6a`; the archive pin has since moved to `bc6464b`.
- **Limit.** Covers three specific packings, not the HKRS families of obstructed packings.
- **Limit.** The result is due to Haag, Kertzer, Rickards and Stange (Ann. of Math. 2024, arXiv:2307.02749); only the zero-Mathlib proof route is new.
- **Limit.** The contrast packing rootSquareContrast = (−4,8,9,9) is only shown to contain 9; HKRS list quadratic (3n², 6n²) and quartic (n⁴, 4n⁴) obstructions for it, so it is not unobstructed (v2.0.0 renamed rootUnobstructed -> rootSquareContrast).
- **Limit.** The mod-24 residue-set comparison is computational, not in Lean.
- **Limit.** The full Apollonian local-global problem remains open.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin (latest release `zenodo-2026-11-28`). They are not covered by this audit.
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`

### R76. Abelian sandpile toppling laws and small-grid Laplacian computations

- **Statement.** For symmetric zero-diagonal adjacency on integer configurations: topplings commute; any legal trace fires each vertex at most w times for a stabilizing odometer w; two legal stabilizing traces have equal counts and results. Via a zero-Mathlib n×n Laplace determinant detMat, Lean proves detMat 4 (gridLap 2) = 192, detMat 9 (gridLap 3) = 100352 (T2b), detMat 4 (a2GridLap 2) = 1092, detMat 9 (a2GridLap 3) = 5393920 (T2f), and legal Z² and A₂ Dhar traces.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`ApollonianSandpileMarkov.Palomar.t2a_abelian_sandpile_confluence_and_least_action`](https://github.com/0thernes/apollonian-sandpile-markov/blob/94ece6a8dce9c9a30c6a2ada2eb335cb0501f770/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L35), [`ApollonianSandpileMarkov.Palomar.t2b_dhar_critical_identity_and_grid_orders`](https://github.com/0thernes/apollonian-sandpile-markov/blob/94ece6a8dce9c9a30c6a2ada2eb335cb0501f770/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L38), [`ApollonianSandpileMarkov.Palomar.t2f_a2_grid_orders_and_dhar_identity`](https://github.com/0thernes/apollonian-sandpile-markov/blob/94ece6a8dce9c9a30c6a2ada2eb335cb0501f770/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L50); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. V2.0.0 proves the 9×9 Z² and A₂ Dirichlet Laplacian determinants directly via zero-Mathlib detMat (replacing the v1.0.0 indirect similarity factorization); the Matrix-Tree / sandpile-group-order interpretation remains outside Lean.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Re-audit pending.** Audited at commit `94ece6a`; the archive pin has since moved to `bc6464b`.
- **Limit.** No sink condition and no termination of stabilization are formalized.
- **Limit.** The 4×4 and 9×9 determinants are proved directly in Lean via detMat (v2.0.0), but the Matrix-Tree theorem and sandpile-group-order identification are not formalized.
- **Limit.** The identity configurations are shown to be stabilizations from Dhar's formula, not proved to be the group identity.
- **Limit.** Abelian property (Dhar 1990) and least action principle are known.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin (latest release `zenodo-2026-11-28`). They are not covered by this audit.

### R77. Fricke-Cohn trace identity and congruences of Markov numbers, including Zhang's mod-32 theorem

- **Statement.** For 2×2 integer matrices of determinant 1, tr(A)² + tr(B)² + tr(AB)² = tr A·tr B·tr AB + tr[A,B] + 2, and Cohn-tree nodes satisfy 3 | tr(A), 3 | tr(B), 3 | tr(AB) and give Markov triples via tr/3. For triples reachable from (1,1,1) by Vieta moves: pairwise coprime; odd prime divisors and odd entries are ≡ 1 (mod 4); even entries are ≡ 2 (mod 32), with 2 and 34 occurring.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`ApollonianSandpileMarkov.Palomar.t3a_sl2z_fricke_cohn_markov_correspondence`](https://github.com/0thernes/apollonian-sandpile-markov/blob/94ece6a8dce9c9a30c6a2ada2eb335cb0501f770/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L53), [`ApollonianSandpileMarkov.Palomar.t3b_markov_coprimality_odd_primes_and_mod32`](https://github.com/0thernes/apollonian-sandpile-markov/blob/94ece6a8dce9c9a30c6a2ada2eb335cb0501f770/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L56); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Mod-32 statement is Zhang, Acta Arith. 128 (2007), arXiv:math/0612620.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement matches the stated claim; prior work: known mathematics.
- **Re-audit pending.** Audited at commit `94ece6a`; the archive pin has since moved to `bc6464b`.
- **Limit.** The mod-32 theorem and its sharpness witnesses were published by Ying Zhang (Acta Arith. 128 (2007), arXiv:math/0612620); v2.0.0 attributes the theorem to Zhang and drops the v1.0.0 'our Exact Mod-32 Theorem' phrasing.
- **Limit.** Statements are for the first coordinate of tree triples; that every positive Markov triple lies in the tree (Markov's theorem) is not formalized.
- **Limit.** The Markov uniqueness conjecture (NT-083) remains open and is not addressed.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin (latest release `zenodo-2026-11-28`). They are not covered by this audit.
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`

### R78. Exchange identities along one five-step mutation sequence of the Markov quiver

- **Statement.** For explicit subtraction-free integer polynomials P₁,…,P₅ in x₁, x₂, x₃: P₁P₄ = x₁⁴x₂²x₃²P₂² + P₃² and P₂P₅ = x₁⁶x₂⁴x₃²P₃² + P₄² identically; each Pᵢ ≥ 1 at positive integer inputs; at (1,1,1) the values are 2, 5, 29, 433, 37666.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declaration [`ApollonianSandpileMarkov.Palomar.t3d_cluster_algebra_markov_laurent_positivity`](https://github.com/0thernes/apollonian-sandpile-markov/blob/94ece6a8dce9c9a30c6a2ada2eb335cb0501f770/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L62); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Positive Laurent coefficients follow by inspection of the definitions, not from a stated theorem.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Re-audit pending.** Audited at commit `94ece6a`; the archive pin has since moved to `bc6464b`.
- **Limit.** One mutation path of depth five; the general Laurent phenomenon (Fomin-Zelevinsky 2002) and positivity (Lee-Schiffler 2015) are known and not formalized.
- **Limit.** Lean's 'positivity' is positivity of values at positive integers.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin (latest release `zenodo-2026-11-28`). They are not covered by this audit.

### R79. Admissible coefficients of the four-variable Markov-Hurwitz equation

- **Statement.** Positive integer solutions of x₁² + x₂² + x₃² + x₄² = a·x₁x₂x₃x₄ exist only for a = 1 (all xᵢ ≡ 2 mod 4) or a = 4 (all xᵢ odd); there are none for a ∈ {2, 3} or a ≥ 5. Explicit solutions are given for a = 1 and a = 4.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declaration [`ApollonianSandpileMarkov.Palomar.t3e_markov_hurwitz_n4_complete_classification`](https://github.com/0thernes/apollonian-sandpile-markov/blob/94ece6a8dce9c9a30c6a2ada2eb335cb0501f770/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L65); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Re-audit pending.** Audited at commit `94ece6a`; the archive pin has since moved to `bc6464b`.
- **Limit.** Classical (Hurwitz 1907, Arch. Math. Phys. 11, 185-196); v2.0.0 cites Hurwitz (1907).
- **Limit.** The description of all solutions as Vieta orbits is not part of the exported statement; v2.0.0 narrows the prose to admissible coefficient classification (keeping the Lean identifier name for comparator continuity).
- **Limit.** Hurwitz equations for n ≥ 5 are not addressed.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin (latest release `zenodo-2026-11-28`). They are not covered by this audit.

### R80. Sedenion box-kite structure of the 42 assessors

- **Statement.** The 42 sedenion pairs (i, j), 1 ≤ i ≤ 7, 9 ≤ j ≤ 15, j ≠ i+8, with adjacency '(e_i+e_j)(e_k ± e_l) = 0 for some sign', form a 4-regular graph that splits into 7 components of 6 vertices, each 4-regular (an octahedron K_{2,2,2}); span{e_0,…,e_8} is norm-multiplicative.
- **Related source.** [R. de Marrais, The 42 Assessors and the Box-Kites They Fly (2000), arXiv:math/0011260](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0011260), abstract (source of the known result, not an open question).
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`CDTerrace.Palomar.prove_t4b`](https://github.com/0thernes/cayley-dickson-terrace-frontier/blob/0ea58439e9f98b4f44f13fa484c5ee4b50badb10/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L37), [`CDTerrace.sedenion_box_kites_7x6`](https://github.com/0thernes/cayley-dickson-terrace-frontier/blob/0ea58439e9f98b4f44f13fa484c5ee4b50badb10/lean/CDTerrace/FiniteCertificates.lean#L1776); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
- **Audit (2026-11-27).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement matches the stated claim; prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** The 42 assessors and the 7 box-kites are due to de Marrais (arXiv:math/0011260, 2000); this is a formal six-kernel re-verification.
- **Limit.** In v2.0.0–v2.1.0, inter-strut disjointness is proved directly from pure vanishing-product adjacency (boxKiteGraphAdj / hasCrossEdgeVtx) linked to cdMulCoordGamma without XOR pre-filtering.
- **Limit.** Norm-multiplicativity of span{e_0,…,e_8} is checked via isNormMultMask 4 511 (cross-term cancellation over basis quadruples).
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin (latest release `zenodo-2026-11-28`). They are not covered by this audit.
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`

- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.

- **Limit.** All headline results are classical or elementary. The Lonely Runner conjecture is proved for up to 13 runners in recent preprints (Rosenfeld, arXiv:2509.14111; Trakulthongchai, arXiv:2511.22427; Sungkawichai and Trakulthongchai, arXiv:2604.23906), far beyond the n ≤ 2 cases and the t = 1/4 subfamily of n = 3 formalized here.
- **Limit.** The n = 3 Lonely Runner item covers 27 of 64 speed-triple classes mod 4, not 7/8 as the prose states.
- **Limit.** The 'ε-invariance barrier' is formalized only as facts about the 3n−1 map; the claim that ε-symmetric arguments cannot settle Collatz is informal.
- **Limit.** Six-kernel replay and lake comparator were not re-run locally; evidence is CI run 45742865067 at the pinned commit.
- **Limit.** Also kernel-checked: 2^n − 1 prime implies n prime (thm_mersenne_exponent_prime).
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin (latest release `zenodo-2026-11-28`). They are not covered by this audit.

<a id="section-f"></a>
## F. Engineering invariant suites

*Machine-checked properties of a software model or simulator. They say the model is internally consistent, not that it describes nature.*

<a id="r43"></a>
### R43. Conservation and monotonicity facts for the repository's discrete vesicle, ATP and SNARE models

- **Statement.** For the repository's definitions: every valid vesicle-pool step list keeps rrp+recycling+reserve; if s<b+f·c, the store (a₀+s·t)∸(b+f·c)·t is below a₀ when a₀,t>0 and is 0 for t≥⌊a₀/D⌋+1, D=b+f·c−s; if b,c>0 and b+f·c≤s, then f·c<s, (s−b)·c<s·c, and ⌊(s−b)/c⌋<⌊s/c⌋ when c≤b; (8n)/8=n; the clamped SNARE barrier is non-increasing in Ca²⁺ and SNARE counts.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`SynapseBouton.vesicle_pool_transition_invariant`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L297), [`SynapseBouton.vesicle_pool_multistep_invariant`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L306), [`SynapseBouton.atp_deficit_strict_depletion`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L319), [`SynapseBouton.atp_hitting_time_upper_bound`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L327), [`SynapseBouton.resting_leak_strictly_lowers_sustainable_rate`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L349), [`SynapseBouton.kinesin_processive_atp_exact`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L364), [`SynapseBouton.snare_barrier_monotone_in_syt1_ca`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L374), [`SynapseBouton.snare_copy_number_cooperativity`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L393); axioms: propext, Quot.sound. True by construction of self-defined update rules; the H3 simulation outcome itself rests on Rust code outside Lean.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** T15 is an upper bound on the zero time, not an exact hitting time; it equals 3 s only for the deterministic mean-rate H3 constants, while the simulator jitters the rate each second.
- **Limit.** The ATP and SNARE constants are the author's and are not found in the cited sources; the Lean definitions are hand-written analogues of the TypeScript/Rust engines with no tested link.
- **Limit.** T17 contains no kinesin model; the SNARE-barrier claims of T18 and T19 are non-strict (T19's only strict part is the zipper energy 115·n₁ < 115·n₂).
- **Limit.** No part of NEURO-001 (consciousness) or NEURO-019 (20 W credit assignment) is addressed.

### R83. Lean 4 model invariants for the PLANARIA .hbin erasure-coded executable format

- **Statement.** In the Lean model: GF(2^8) arithmetic mod 0x11D forms a field; the 2×2 Cauchy code decodes exactly for distinct coordinates ≥ 2 (k = 2 only); the fixed schedule gives each half ≥ k+2 cells per bundle; a burst of ≤ 16 bytes touches ≤ 8 even and ≤ 8 odd positions; a quorum with two tied maximal buckets of count ≥ 2 returns none; RAM masking stays below 4096; CNOT preserves the squared norm.

- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** Cauchy decoding is proved only for k = 2; bundles with k in {4, 6, 8, 16} rely on the classical Cauchy determinant theorem and tests.
- **Limit.** No Reed-Solomon code or decoder is formalized; the 8-errors-per-lane radius is arithmetic on 254 − 238 + 1.
- **Limit.** The Merkle quarantine theorem assumes an authenticity-root correspondence (HashBinding) rather than deriving it from a hash.
- **Limit.** The JavaScript runtime, Python oracle and survival benchmarks lie outside Lean.
- **Limit.** The field laws, Cauchy inversion and counting bounds are textbook mathematics; no open problem is addressed.
- **Limit.** The quorum result also needs every other bucket to be at most the tied count; lanes are modelled as even and odd byte positions.
- **Limit.** The scaled Hadamard doubles the squared norm (hadamardScaled4Q_normSq4), so 'integer-amplitude gates preserve the squared norm' holds for CNOT, not for H.

- **Limit.** Several counted theorems are literal arithmetic identities or restate a hypothesis.
- **Limit.** Six-kernel replay is CI-only (Linux bubblewrap) and was not re-run in this audit.
- **Limit.** Bounds need the stated input ranges, for example CSS ≤ 10000 when difficulty, centrality and age are ≤ 100, and Titan in [90, 1000] when difficulty, impact and interdisciplinarity are in [1, 10] and the degree term is ≤ 100.
- **Limit.** The 7-layer list has a size theorem only, and the era map has monotonicity and samples but no iff characterisation.
- **Limit.** AQS has a bound but is shown monotone in only three of its five inputs, so AQS monotonicity is not claimed.
- **Limit.** The handshaking lemma needs a duplicate-free vertex list that contains every edge endpoint.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin. They are not covered by this audit.

### R86. Discrete invariant suite for the Cellular Engine Omega software model

- **Statement.** Lean 4.35.0 lemmas over Nat, Int and List about the engine's discrete software model: commutation of pointwise updates at distinct indices of a Nat→Int map and list-sum conservation under local steps, an integer projection that zeroes a list sum, 2×2 integer Jacobian sign algebra, Nat power inequalities, closed arithmetic checks on hard-coded constants, and equalities among C11-exported receipt literals (O63, O72); 100 audited items.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`OmegaCellular.BioInteractionNets.O42_active_pair_diamond_strong_confluence`](https://github.com/0thernes/cellular-engine-omega/blob/4b257af5f2659ab29a29dc026a17d1c92d011ace/lean/OmegaCellularProofs/BioInteractionNets.lean#L31), [`OmegaCellular.VirtualCellManifold.O56_virtual_cell_physics_projection_conservation`](https://github.com/0thernes/cellular-engine-omega/blob/4b257af5f2659ab29a29dc026a17d1c92d011ace/lean/OmegaCellularProofs/VirtualCellManifold.lean#L45), [`OmegaCellular.EigenProofreadingInfo.O06_hopfield_ninio_proofreading_beats_equilibrium`](https://github.com/0thernes/cellular-engine-omega/blob/4b257af5f2659ab29a29dc026a17d1c92d011ace/lean/OmegaCellularProofs/EigenProofreadingInfo.lean#L18), [`OmegaCellular.TuringFeinbergCRNT.O12_turing_equal_diffusion_impossibility`](https://github.com/0thernes/cellular-engine-omega/blob/4b257af5f2659ab29a29dc026a17d1c92d011ace/lean/OmegaCellularProofs/TuringFeinbergCRNT.lean#L21), [`OmegaCellular.VerifyTraceReceipt.O63_live_c11_receipt_verified`](https://github.com/0thernes/cellular-engine-omega/blob/4b257af5f2659ab29a29dc026a17d1c92d011ace/lean/OmegaCellularProofs/VerifyTraceReceipt.lean#L90), [`OmegaCellular.SubstratesCube.O72_live_c11_cube_receipt_verified`](https://github.com/0thernes/cellular-engine-omega/blob/4b257af5f2659ab29a29dc026a17d1c92d011ace/lean/OmegaCellularProofs/SubstratesCube.lean#L34); axioms: propext, Quot.sound. Receipt values come from one C11 run outside Lean; floating-point solvers and C memory safety are tested empirically, not proved.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: not yet searched.
- **Limit.** The lemmas concern the integer software model; no biological or continuum-physics law (Poincaré–Hopf, Turing instability, TUR) is formalized in general.
- **Limit.** At least 16 of the 100 items are closed arithmetic checks on literals, for example 661 + 274 + 20 + 45 = 1000.
- **Limit.** O63 and O72 check equalities among literals written by one C11 run at seed 2026001; no hash is verified in Lean.
- **Limit.** Independent-checker and comparator runs were confirmed only through CI run 45810663954, not reproduced locally.
- **Limit.** Solves no open problem; the repository states 0/1,900 Mega-Atlas problems retired.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin. They are not covered by this audit.
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [cellular-engine-omega](https://github.com/0thernes/cellular-engine-omega) `v5.3.0` · archive entry `0TH-BUILD-008` · [paper](builds/0TH-BUILD-008_cellular-engine-omega/Donahue_2026_cellular_engine_omega.pdf)

### R87. Kernel-checked finite-field and bitvector invariants of the AUTOPHAGE engine model

- **Statement.** For the repository's Lean models: under a trial-division irreducibility test (divisors of degree 1–4), exactly 30 of the 256 polynomials x⁸+p over F₂ pass, and they match the 30-entry table in src/galois_math.c; for each, the 2×2 Cauchy code [[1,3],[5,1]] recovers both data bytes from the two parity bytes; affine GF(2) maps with linear inverses round-trip; Fredkin conserves popcount; masked-XOR kinship is transitive; multi-step integer ledgers keep a zero residual.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`Autophage.T12a_full_trial_div_matches_c11_table`](https://github.com/0thernes/autophage/blob/1956c2cc54845ebadc54b2a5276cbc66bf031a8b/lean/AutophageProofs.lean#L614), [`Autophage.T16_planarian_50pct_exact_recovery`](https://github.com/0thernes/autophage/blob/1956c2cc54845ebadc54b2a5276cbc66bf031a8b/lean/AutophageProofs.lean#L771), [`Autophage.T05_weismann_exact_roundtrip`](https://github.com/0thernes/autophage/blob/1956c2cc54845ebadc54b2a5276cbc66bf031a8b/lean/AutophageProofs.lean#L172), [`Autophage.T20a_fredkin64_popcnt_conserved`](https://github.com/0thernes/autophage/blob/1956c2cc54845ebadc54b2a5276cbc66bf031a8b/lean/AutophageProofs.lean#L876), [`Autophage.T25_ultrametric_strong_triangle`](https://github.com/0thernes/autophage/blob/1956c2cc54845ebadc54b2a5276cbc66bf031a8b/lean/AutophageProofs.lean#L907), [`Autophage.T29a_first_law_ledger_multistep`](https://github.com/0thernes/autophage/blob/1956c2cc54845ebadc54b2a5276cbc66bf031a8b/lean/AutophageProofs.lean#L984); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Facts about Lean definitions, not the emitted x86-64 code; several of the 48 theorems are one-line arithmetic identities.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** The theorems are about Lean models; JIT machine-code emission, C11 memory safety and FP64 drift are checked only by tests.
- **Limit.** T21, T28, T29 and T30 are tautologies (for example sink ≤ sink + rad) despite Landauer, First-Law and Second-Law names.
- **Limit.** The count of 30 irreducible binary octics and the reversible-gate identities are textbook results.
- **Limit.** No open problem, including AI-045 or BIO-001, is resolved; biological terms are metaphors (LIMITATIONS.md sec. 1).
- **Limit.** Six-kernel acceptance was confirmed from the CI log only; replay needs Linux bubblewrap.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin. They are not covered by this audit.
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`

### R88. Lean invariants for a ten-pool integer energy-ledger model and helper encodings

- **Statement.** In the Lean model of a ten-field unbounded-integer ledger: guarded ATP→heat, patch→gut and ATP→tissue transfers, the equal-amount pair ATP→neural then neural→heat, and the composite tick built from them leave the field sum unchanged; ATP→heat never lowers the heat field and preserves non-negativity of all fields. Also: a region<4 edit guard returns its input, 2-bit ternary encoding round-trips on {−1,0,1}, 2·(1+2+…+n)=n(n+1), 16·2^Q≤16384 for Q≤10, and hard-coded receipt constants satisfy stated equalities and bounds.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`NoeticProofs.N01_atp_to_heat_conserves_sum`](https://github.com/0thernes/noetic-organism-omega/blob/c4301d926fa12334f8f8f54b2994dfc12ff649b8/lean/NoeticProofs.lean#L20), [`NoeticProofs.N09_closed_tick_exact_conservation`](https://github.com/0thernes/noetic-organism-omega/blob/c4301d926fa12334f8f8f54b2994dfc12ff649b8/lean/NoeticProofs.lean#L89), - **Limit.** No consciousness, cognition, biology or physics result is shown; 29 cognitive checks are indicator-only by the repository's own statement.

- **Limit.** The added N02, N04, N05 and N07 depend on propext and Quot.sound, like N01.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin. They are not covered by this audit.

### R89. Arithmetic conservation and addressing checks for an abstract model of an artificial-life engine

- **Statement.** In the engine's Lean model over ℕ: moving dm≤bioMass from biomass to cell mass, or de≤bioEnergy to heat, preserves the respective total; for cur≤cap a capped receive splits q into kept+rejected=q with cur+kept≤cap; six face fluxes each ≤amt/8 sum to ≤amt; converting k≤nutXMass weight-24 units into weight-16 biomass plus thermal energy preserves weighted energy; for uid<2^32, tkey0 xor (uid/2^32)=tkey0, but not universally; offsets 8·n are injective and below 32 GiB for n<2^32.

Statements concern Spec.lean definitions only; the C23/NASM/PTX implementation is checked by tests outside Lean.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: not yet searched.
- **Limit.** The Lean definitions are not linked to the C23, NASM or CUDA PTX code; only constants are copied by hand.
- **Limit.** The flux theorem assumes a per-face amt/8 cap, while core/az_chem.c uses a per-species a/4 total budget.
- **Limit.** About 14 of the 30 suite theorems (A06-A16, A18-A20) are constant identities, literal arithmetic, definitional or restated hypotheses and are not part of this record.
- **Limit.** Axioms shown are the union over the listed declarations; A21 alone needs Classical.choice, A30 only propext.
- **Limit.** No open problem is addressed; the repository reports 0 of 1,900 Mega-Atlas problems retired.
- **Limit.** All quantities are natural numbers; the hypotheses dm ≤ bioMass, de ≤ bioEnergy and k ≤ nutXMass rule out truncated subtraction.
- **Limit.** In the conversion clause each converted unit adds the 24 − 16 = 8 surplus to thermal energy; that term is what makes the weighted total balance.
- **Limit.** The xor refutation is proved with the single witness tkey0 = 0, uid = 2^32.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin. They are not covered by this audit.

### R93. Integer ledger and carbon-nitrogen trace conservation and capped-simplex bounds for an artificial-life model

- **Statement.** In the ALife software's integer Lean model: finite transfer/import/export traces leave the 11-pool residual total−(initial+imports−exports) unchanged; finite assimilate/shed/mineralize traces conserve total C and total N; each assimilation step changes biomass C by exactly 4 times its biomass N change; any 7 natural weights summing to 10000, each ≤4800, are all <5000 with at least 3 nonzero; plus Pythagoras for orthogonal equal-length integer lists, 2p³<p⁴ for p≥3, and arithmetic on hard-coded constants.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`ALifeProofs.LedgerConservation.applyTrace_preserves_residual`](https://github.com/0thernes/ALife-Framework/blob/48a2a0aa2baeea1e430c2134a7b963a7cf67727b/lean/ALifeProofs/LedgerConservation.lean#L234), [`ALifeProofs.Stoichiometry.applyBioTrace_conserves_CN`](https://github.com/0thernes/ALife-Framework/blob/48a2a0aa2baeea1e430c2134a7b963a7cf67727b/lean/ALifeProofs/Stoichiometry.lean#L122), [`ALifeProofs.Stoichiometry.assimilate4to1_exact_ratio`](https://github.com/0thernes/ALife-Framework/blob/48a2a0aa2baeea1e430c2134a7b963a7cf67727b/lean/ALifeProofs/Stoichiometry.lean#L97), [`ALifeProofs.HeptarchSimplex.no_single_seat_majority`](https://github.com/0thernes/ALife-Framework/blob/48a2a0aa2baeea1e430c2134a7b963a7cf67727b/lean/ALifeProofs/HeptarchSimplex.lean#L79), [`ALifeProofs.HeptarchSimplex.capped_simplex_at_least_three_active`](https://github.com/0thernes/ALife-Framework/blob/48a2a0aa2baeea1e430c2134a7b963a7cf67727b/lean/ALifeProofs/HeptarchSimplex.lean#L90), [`ALifeProofs.TensorAndCoding.hodge_pythagorean_conservation`](https://github.com/0thernes/ALife-Framework/blob/48a2a0aa2baeea1e430c2134a7b963a7cf67727b/lean/ALifeProofs/TensorAndCoding.lean#L144), [`ALifeProofs.TensorAndCoding.monarch_strictly_smaller_for_p_ge_3`](https://github.com/0thernes/ALife-Framework/blob/48a2a0aa2baeea1e430c2134a7b963a7cf67727b/lean/ALifeProofs/TensorAndCoding.lean#L77), [`ALifeProofs.Solution.prove_all_alife_invariants`](https://github.com/0thernes/ALife-Framework/blob/48a2a0aa2baeea1e430c2134a7b963a7cf67727b/lean/Solution.lean#L77); axioms: propext, Quot.sound. Lean models are not linked to the TypeScript/WASM runtime. Contextuality, Reed-Solomon and registry entries check only hard-coded constants.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** The theorems are about a separate integer Lean model. No proof links it to the float64 TypeScript/WASM runtime.
- **Limit.** The contextuality (Hoggar, KCBS, Tsirelson, srg Jordan gap), RS[15,11], 75-substrate, 1,000-cube and 825-check entries are arithmetic on hard-coded constants, not formalized structures.
- **Limit.** The CEGA-18 lemma assumes the double-counting identity as a hypothesis and never builds the 18 rays.
- **Limit.** 'Second Law' and 'WCAG clamp' are definitional (isDonorPool, min x 3000); no entropy or rendered-flash property is proved.
- **Limit.** No open problem is retired (0/1,900 Mega-Atlas); the mathematics is elementary.
- **Limit.** The six-kernel acceptance was seen in CI run 45824894491 but not re-run locally (it needs Linux bubblewrap).
- **Limit.** Ledger transfers are guarded only by pool indices and a non-negative amount, so donor pools may become negative.
- **Limit.** The 4:1 ratio is a single-step fact that holds trivially when the assimilation guard fails; shed and mineralize steps move C and N independently.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin. They are not covered by this audit.
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean ALifeProofs/VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [ALife-Framework](https://github.com/0thernes/ALife-Framework) `v3.0.0` · archive entry `0TH-BUILD-016` · [paper](builds/0TH-BUILD-016_ALife-Framework/Donahue_2026_alife_framework_v3.pdf)

## Not claimed

- No Millennium Prize problem and no grand open problem is solved here. P versus NP is open.
- No result has been refereed by a journal or checked by a named outside expert.
- Engineering invariant suites (section F) verify software models. They are not evidence about consciousness, sentience, biology or physics.
- A search that found no earlier proof is not a proof of novelty.

## How a result gets on this list

1. The claim is registered in the archive with a pinned commit and a frozen paper.
2. The formal statement is read against the informal claim and against the cited source, in a session that did not write the proof.
3. The proof is rebuilt from a clean clone at that commit, or the ledger says it was not.
4. The literature is searched for earlier or parallel proofs and the outcome is recorded.
5. The wording is limited to what steps 2 to 4 support. Anything narrower than the usual informal claim is stated under Limit.

## How to challenge a result

- Open an issue on this repository or on the result's repository and quote the result number (for example R7).
- A reproducible counterexample, a gap in a statement audit, or an earlier proof in the literature leads to a correction: the result is narrowed, reclassified or withdrawn, and keeps its number.
- Corrections are recorded in CHANGELOG.md.

## What Would Prove Us Wrong (Falsification Protocol)

Any failing run of `python3 scripts/verify_archive.py`, `sha256sum -c CHECKSUMS.sha256`, or `python3 -m pytest -v tests/` immediately falsifies the corresponding integrity claim above. External critics can also independently clone any pinned submodule at its exact commit SHA and run the entry's `falsification_command` from `EVIDENCE.md`.

<!-- FILE: LIMITATIONS.md -->

# Limitations, Epistemic Boundaries & Real-vs-Metaphor (`LIMITATIONS.md`)

## 1. What This Master Archive Does and Does Not Guarantee

- **Cryptographic provenance, NOT external peer review:** `0thernes-research-archive` cryptographically locks frozen PDFs, exact Git submodule commits, Lean 4 axiom policies, and CI run links. None of the archived research preprints have undergone external journal peer review unless explicitly recorded with a publisher DOI.
- **No Mega-Atlas grand-problem retirement claimed:** As documented in [`RESULTS.md`](RESULTS.md) and [`registry/SOLVED_AND_ATLAS_BRIDGE.md`](registry/SOLVED_AND_ATLAS_BRIDGE.md) (the archived upstream audit `builds/0TH-BUILD-007_unsolved-problems-mega-atlas/0THERNES_SOLVED_AUDIT_2026-11-25.md` predates the 2026-11-26 statement audit and still says two Vinciguerra questions are resolved), **0 of 2,000** grand open problems in `unsolved-problems-mega-atlas` (`v2.10.0`; `0 of 1,900` in the earlier `v2.5.0` snapshot) are retired by entries in this archive; specialized theorems (such as Conjecture 7.7 of Banić & Elezović in `0TH-2026-006`) are proved within their exact cited scopes.
- **Historical snapshots vs. live repos:** Superseded repositories (`0TH-2026-001`, `002`, `003`, `005`) remain pinned as immutable historical snapshots for provenance while active unified research continues in `0TH-2026-009` (`pauli-contextuality-lab`). Historical `METADATA.json` records may retain earlier version metadata as frozen snapshots.
- **AI-assisted provenance:** Individual papers and builds were produced by solo researcher Alexander Stephen Donahue (`Independent Researcher, Spokane, WA, USA`, ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`) with disclosed AI assistance; epistemic trust rests on reproducible kernel verification and falsification commands in each entry's `EVIDENCE.md`.

## 2. Real vs. Metaphor

- **"Vault" / "Frozen":** Literally means committed Git blobs hashed with SHA-256 inside `CHECKSUMS.sha256` and verified on every push by GitHub Actions CI.
- **"Tier I / Tier II / Tier III":** Strict epistemic separation: Tier I holds standalone research preprints; Tier II holds engineering build white papers and embedded Pure Lean invariant suites; Tier III holds architectural laws, pre-registered empirical claims (including null results), finite computational certificates, and open-problem atlases—never conflated with Lean-proved general mathematical theorems.

<!-- FILE: REPLICATION.md -->

# Replication Protocol (`REPLICATION.md`)

Any third party can verify the entire canonical master archive, live ecosystem mirror, Mega-Atlas bridge, and DigiCert RFC 3161 TSA release seal from a clean clone:

```bash
# 1. Clone the archive (add --recursive to fetch every pinned public submodule).
#    Needs Python 3.10 or newer: the pinned test tools do not install on 3.9. CI uses 3.12.
git clone https://github.com/0thernes/0thernes-research-archive.git
cd 0thernes-research-archive
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt

# 2. Verify every SHA-256 digest, RFC 3161 TSA seal, ORCID, axiom policy, bridge parity, table continuity,
#    zero broken links, every submodule pin, and the numbered Results Ledger (RESULTS.md)
python3 scripts/verify_archive.py
sha256sum -c CHECKSUMS.sha256
python3 scripts/build_ledger.py --check

# 3. Run automated integrity, privacy-firewall, failure-injection, property, negative, mutation & idempotence tests
python3 -m pytest -v tests/
python3 scripts/build_site.py
bash scripts/audit-repo.sh .
```

To refresh the live upstream status mirror against GitHub right now, run `python3 scripts/live_sync.py`. To verify a specific paper's Lean 4 formal proof from scratch, run `git submodule update --init repos/<slug>` and execute the exact `falsification_command` printed in `papers/<id>/EVIDENCE.md`.

# AGENTS.md — Canonical Agent Instructions (`0thernes-research-archive`)

This file is the canonical instruction file for all AI agents (`CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, and `.cursor/rules/build-standard.mdc` point here).

## Mission & Identity

- **Repository:** `https://github.com/0thernes/0thernes-research-archive`
- **Author:** Alexander Stephen Donahue (`Independent Researcher, Spokane, WA, USA`, ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`, `0_0@0thernes.art`). Do NOT assert an unformed LLC entity in new headers or metadata.
- **Privacy Firewall (MANDATORY):** NEVER register, mention, or submodule private repositories or third-party forks. Every entry MUST be `PUBLIC`.

## Hard Rules (`R1`–`R8`)

1. Commit and push straight to `main` (`R1`/`R2`); CI is informational (`R3`); zero banned files such as `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` or `dependabot.yml` (`R4`).
2. Never fabricate SHA-256 digests, CI run URLs, DOIs, or peer-review status (`R6`).
3. Always run `python3 scripts/verify_archive.py --sync` after updating any PDF, artifact, or submodule pin, and copy `CHECKSUMS.sha256` to `data/MANIFEST.sha256`.
4. Classify every defect into one of the 10 Build Standard classes (`R7`; `docs/glossary.md`).

## Core Commands

```bash
just reproduce   # Verify archive, checksums, pytest suite, static site, and Build Standard audit
just sync        # Regenerate METADATA.json, EVIDENCE.md, registry/*.md, CHECKSUMS.sha256, data/MANIFEST.sha256
just test        # Run pytest integrity/property/negative/mutation suite
just audit       # Score repo against Build Standard v1.2.0
```

# Solved Sub-Conjectures & Mega-Atlas V2 Cross-Reference Bridge

**Audit Date:** `2026-11-27` · **Author:** Alexander Stephen Donahue (Independent Researcher, Spokane, WA, USA, ORCID [`0009-0006-8168-9648`](https://orcid.org/0009-0006-8168-9648))  
**Mega-Atlas grand problems retired by this work:** **`0 / 2000`**  
**Open questions from arXiv preprints answered in Lean 4.35.0:** **2** (+ 1 with a step cited from outside Lean). None of the sources or proofs is peer reviewed; the numbered list with statements and limits is [`RESULTS.md`](../RESULTS.md).

> **Epistemic Boundary:** 0 of the 2,000 catalogued problems in the Unsolved Problems Mega-Atlas are solved by this work. Two entries answer a question that another author stated as open in an arXiv preprint: Conjecture 7.7 of Banić and Elezović (arXiv:2610.17046v1) in 0TH-2026-006, and the limit question of Section 6 of Muller and Saniga (arXiv:2609.19862v1) in 0TH-2026-009 Track 2, where the identification of the formal objects with the preprint's hypergraphs rests partly on argument outside Lean. 0TH-2026-009 Track 1 also proves strict-law failure for one representative of each case of Jonah's Conjecture E from an unreviewed Zenodo preprint, with Theorem B4 cited from outside Lean. Neither these sources nor these proofs are peer reviewed. Each row's class follows the strongest kind among its results in RESULTS.md. Of the other 27 rows, 5 are new-theorem suites, 2 bounded or partial cases, 7 formalizations of known results (1 of them a barrier formalization) and 13 invariant suites of software models. Entries without a machine-checked result at their pinned commit have no row; RESULTS.md lists them with the reason.

## How this mirror is refreshed

- **Scheduled pull (active):** [`.github/workflows/live-sync.yml`](../.github/workflows/live-sync.yml) queries the GitHub API every hour (`17 * * * *`), re-verifies SHA-256 integrity and `pytest`, and commits only when upstream state changed. GitHub may start scheduled runs late, so this table can lag the source repositories by an hour or more. The `Synced (UTC)` stamp above is the time of the last change, not of the last check.
- **Manual refresh (active):** run the workflow by hand (`workflow_dispatch`) or `python scripts/live_sync.py` locally.
- **Push dispatch (optional, needs setup):** an upstream repository with [`docs/upstream-notify-workflow.yml`](../docs/upstream-notify-workflow.yml) installed as `.github/workflows/notify-archive.yml` and an `ARCHIVE_SYNC_TOKEN` secret triggers a refresh on every push to `main`. Without the secret the workflow skips the dispatch, and the hourly pull still applies.
- **Discovery inventory:** [`PUBLIC_REPO_INVENTORY.md`](PUBLIC_REPO_INVENTORY.md) lists every public, non-fork owner repository and marks unregistered repositories as candidates without promoting them into the epistemic archive.
- **Immutability rule:** Release-pinned frozen PDFs and Rekor-attested submodules are only advanced when matching frozen artifacts are archived; post-release upstream commits appear immediately as `AHEAD_OF_PIN` with live CI links.

<!-- FILE: docs/architecture.md -->

# Archive Architecture (`docs/architecture.md`)

`0thernes-research-archive` is the **single canonical public master hub** organizing all public scientific outputs authored by Alexander Stephen Donahue (`ORCID 0009-0006-8168-9648`) into **three strictly separated epistemic tiers** (**58 entries**: 29 Tier I + 17 Tier II + 12 Tier III), backed by **45 pinned public Git submodules** under `repos/`, a **94-result audited Results Ledger** (`RESULTS.md` generated from `registry/RESULTS_LEDGER.json`), a **28-row Solved Sub-Conjectures & Mega-Atlas V2 Bridge**, an **hourly-refreshed Upstream Ecosystem Mirror** (the current count is generated in `registry/LIVE_ECOSYSTEM_MIRROR.json` and `registry/PUBLIC_REPO_INVENTORY.json`), a unified SHA-256 integrity manifest (`CHECKSUMS.sha256` & `data/MANIFEST.sha256`), and an immutable DigiCert RFC 3161 TSA–sealed frozen release manifest (`data/RELEASE_FREEZE.sha256` + `data/RELEASE_FREEZE.sha256.tsr`).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UP["Upstream Public 0thernes/* Repos (50 tracked)"] -->|hourly cron; repository_dispatch optional, not configured| LS["scripts/live_sync.py"]
    R1["registry/PAPERS.json<br/>Tier I: 29 Standalone Preprints"] --> V["scripts/verify_archive.py"]
    R2["registry/BUILD_PAPERS.json<br/>Tier II: 17 Builds · 1,119 Lean Decls at pins"] --> V
    R3["registry/LAWS_AND_DISCOVERIES.json<br/>Tier III: 12 Laws, Claims & Atlases"] --> V
    RL["registry/RESULTS_LEDGER.json<br/>94 Audited Results"] --> BL["scripts/build_ledger.py -> RESULTS.md"]
    BL --> V
    BR["registry/SOLVED_AND_ATLAS_BRIDGE.json<br/>0/1900 Grand · 3 Answered Preprint Questions"] --> V
    LS --> LM["registry/LIVE_ECOSYSTEM_MIRROR.json/.md & PUBLIC_REPO_INVENTORY.json"]
    LM --> V
    PR["scripts/privacy.py<br/>Hashed Privacy Firewall"] --> V
    S["repos/* (45 Pinned Public Submodules)"] --> V
    V --> C["CHECKSUMS.sha256 & data/MANIFEST.sha256"]
    V --> FZ["data/RELEASE_FREEZE.sha256 + DigiCert .tsr"]
    V --> D["Per-Entry METADATA.json + EVIDENCE.md"]
    V --> P["scripts/build_site.py -> WCAG 2.2 AA Pages Portal"]
```

## Verification Invariants

1. **Single-script deterministic derivation (`scripts/verify_archive.py --sync`):** Regenerates all `METADATA.json`, `EVIDENCE.md`, `registry/*.md`, `CHECKSUMS.sha256`, `data/MANIFEST.sha256`, and `data/RELEASE_FREEZE.sha256` directly from the canonical JSON registries (verified idempotent by B14 tests).
2. **Audited Results Ledger (`scripts/build_ledger.py --check`):** Deterministically renders `RESULTS.md` from `registry/RESULTS_LEDGER.json` (94 audited results across Sections A–F), checks schema/prior-work/promotional-language/staleness invariants, and enforces full Tier I + Tier II coverage ([ADR 0003](adr/0003-numbered-results-ledger.md)).
3. **Scheduled upstream mirror (`scripts/live_sync.py` + `.github/workflows/live-sync.yml`, hourly):** Tracks live `main` HEADs, latest releases, and CI status across every tracked public non-fork `0thernes/*` repository (count in `registry/LIVE_ECOSYSTEM_MIRROR.json`) without disturbing immutable release-pinned frozen PDFs or invalidating `data/RELEASE_FREEZE.sha256.tsr`.
4. **Exact submodule commit pinning, table continuity, prose count parity & A24 size caps:** Every `pinned_commit` in `PAPERS.json` and `BUILD_PAPERS.json` matches `git ls-files --stage repos` (`45` submodules), `README.md` registry tables cannot be split by blank lines, prose counts across all `COUNT_GUARDED_FILES` (including `HARDENING_INDEX.md` and `docs/architecture.md`) match exact registry totals, `SOLVED_AND_ATLAS_BRIDGE.json` enforces exact version parity against the registries, and every archived file is strictly `< 5 MB`.
5. **Strict axiom, identity, link, TSA & ORCID enforcement:** Every entry carries ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`, zero unformed `"0thernes LLC"` assertions, an explicit `verification_boundary`, Lean axiom allowlists strictly within `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, valid DigiCert RFC 3161 TSA digest binding, and zero broken relative markdown links in hub-authored files.
6. **Public-only privacy firewall (`scripts/privacy.py`):** Zero private repositories or third-party forks may appear anywhere in `registry/`, `repos/`, `llms.txt`, `docs/`, or `.gitmodules`, verified using salted SHA-256 digests so private slugs never appear in plaintext.

<!-- FILE: docs/adr/0001-three-tier-epistemic-archive.md -->

# ADR 0001: Three-Tier Epistemic Separation and Pinned Submodule Vault Architecture

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-21 (formalized in ADR format 2026-11-25)

## Context
A single researcher producing both standalone machine-checked mathematical preprints, engineering systems with embedded formal invariant proofs, and empirical/exploratory open-problem atlases risks conflating distinct levels of proof rigor if all artifacts sit in one flat bibliography.

## Decision
Separate the public master archive into three machine-readable registries (`registry/PAPERS.json`, `registry/BUILD_PAPERS.json`, `registry/LAWS_AND_DISCOVERIES.json`), require an explicit `verification_boundary` on every entry, pin every public source repository as an exact Git submodule under `repos/`, and lock every frozen artifact with byte-exact SHA-256 digests (`CHECKSUMS.sha256` & `data/MANIFEST.sha256`) verified on every push.

## Consequences
- Readers and auditors can immediately distinguish Lean 4 research proofs (Tier I; six-kernel checks cover each repository's comparator targets, or all default targets where CI runs `lake check --paranoid`) from engineering invariant suites (Tier II) and empirical/atlas registries (Tier III).
- Any upstream tampering or accidental submodule drift immediately fails `scripts/verify_archive.py`.


---

<!-- FILE: docs/adr/0002-canonical-hub-and-live-sync.md -->

# ADR 0002: Single Canonical Public Hub, Atlas Consolidation, and Real-Time Live Sync

- **Status:** Accepted (`2026-11-25`)
- **Author:** Alexander Stephen Donahue (Independent Researcher, Spokane, WA, USA; ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`)
- **Supersedes:** Scattered ad-hoc manual synchronization across specialist catalogues

## Context

Across the `0thernes` GitHub ecosystem, five repositories previously appeared to act as overlapping "lists or archives":

1. `0thernes/0thernes-research-archive` — Public cryptographic master vault of all Tier I preprints, Tier II build white papers & Lean 4 suites, and Tier III laws/discoveries/atlases.
2. `0thernes/unsolved-problems-mega-atlas` — Cross-disciplinary 1,900-problem open-problems connectome (`0TH-BUILD-007`).
3. `0thernes/unsolved-mathematics` — Mathematics-focused open-problem atlas and 8-domain Lean 4 structural core (`0TH-BUILD-004`, `0TH-DISC-005`).
4. `0thernes/unsolved-black-hole-problems` — 16-problem ranked black-hole physics catalogue (`0TH-DISC-006`).
5. Private research staging repositories (strictly non-public; never referenced or indexed in public vaults).

Without a unified live-sync layer and cross-atlas bridge, readers and agents had to inspect multiple repositories to answer basic questions: *"Which repository is the authoritative master list?"*, *"Which upstream repos have moved ahead of their frozen release pin?"*, and *"Have any of the 1,900 Mega-Atlas problems or smaller peer-literature conjectures been formally proved?"*

## Decision

1. **Single Canonical Public Hub:** Establish `0thernes/0thernes-research-archive` (and its GitHub Pages portal `https://0thernes.github.io/0thernes-research-archive/`) as the **one authoritative public master hub**. Specialist open-problem catalogues remain focused domain spokes indexed inside Tier II / Tier III and link back to the hub.
2. **Authoritative Solved-Subconjecture & Mega-Atlas Bridge:** Maintain `registry/SOLVED_AND_ATLAS_BRIDGE.json` (and derived `.md`) inside this hub, explicitly enforcing `grand_problems_retired = 0 / 1900` while indexing every machine-checked peer-literature sub-conjecture, bounded partial result, barrier formalization, and discrete invariant suite.
3. **Hybrid Pull + Push Real-Time Live Sync (Preserving Release Immutability):**
   - **Pull-based scheduled mirror (zero secrets required):** `.github/workflows/live-sync.yml` runs `scripts/live_sync.py` every 2 hours (`0 */2 * * *`) using the standard `GITHUB_TOKEN` to refresh `registry/LIVE_ECOSYSTEM_MIRROR.json/.md`, update `README.md`'s bounded live status block, re-run `verify_archive.py --sync` + `pytest`, and commit straight to `main` (which immediately redeploys GitHub Pages).
   - **Push-based instant dispatch (opt-in):** Upstream repos carrying `.github/workflows/notify-archive.yml` (template in `docs/upstream-notify-workflow.yml`) fire `repository_dispatch` (`upstream-repo-updated`) on every `main` push once `ARCHIVE_SYNC_TOKEN` is configured.
   - **Why we do NOT inject commits into already-attested Tier I release repos:** Pushing cosmetic workflow files onto completed, Sigstore/Rekor-attested releases would break `HEAD == release_tag` parity and trigger redundant 20-minute 6-kernel CI runs. The 2-hour scheduled pull mirror already tracks every public repo automatically without disturbing immutable release tags.
4. **Strict Public-Only Privacy Firewall:** `scripts/live_sync.py` rejects any repository where `private == true`, `fork == true`, or `owner != 0thernes`, enforced both at runtime and in `tests/test_archive_integrity.py`.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** One single canonical source of truth, automatically refreshed live mirror and GitHub Pages portal, zero broken cross-atlas links, and strict separation between immutable frozen release pins and live upstream `main` HEADs.
- **Trade-off:** Instant sub-minute push updates require setting one optional `ARCHIVE_SYNC_TOKEN` secret on upstream repos; without it, sync latency is bounded by the 2-hour schedule (or instant via manual `workflow_dispatch`).

## Update (2026-11-26): what is actually running

An audit of the workflow history and the upstream repositories on 2026-11-26 found that the push path had never fired: 0 of the hub's sync runs were started by `repository_dispatch`, 2 of the 41 tracked repositories carried a notify workflow, and none had the `ARCHIVE_SYNC_TOKEN` secret. The mirror is therefore a scheduled pull, and calling it "real-time" overstated it. Changes made:

- The schedule moved from every 2 hours to hourly (`17 * * * *`; minute 17 avoids the top-of-hour queue, where GitHub delays scheduled runs most).
- Generated and hand-written text now says "refreshed hourly" and states that push dispatch is optional and not configured.
- The mirror's `synced_utc` stamp is the time of the last change in upstream state, not of the last check; the generated page says so.

Push-triggered refresh remains available as an owner action: create one fine-grained token that may send `repository_dispatch` to this repository, and store it as `ARCHIVE_SYNC_TOKEN` in each upstream repository that carries the notify workflow. Tokens are never created or stored by automation in this repository. The numbered results list ([ADR 0003](0003-numbered-results-ledger.md)) does not depend on this path: it joins versions and pins from the registries on every sync and marks results whose source has moved past the audited commit.


---

<!-- FILE: docs/adr/0003-numbered-results-ledger.md -->

# ADR 0003: One Numbered Results Ledger

- **Status:** Accepted (`2026-11-26`)
- **Author:** Alexander Stephen Donahue (Independent Researcher, Spokane, WA, USA; ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`)
- **Builds on:** [ADR 0002](0002-canonical-hub-and-live-sync.md) (single canonical hub and live sync)

## Context

The hub answers "which repositories exist and are they intact". It did not answer, in one readable place, "what exactly has been proven". That information was spread across long table cells in `README.md`, the Mega-Atlas bridge and each paper, written per repository rather than per result, and mixed with build and provenance detail. A reader could not see a plain list of results, and a claim's wording was never tied to an audit of the statement itself.

## Decision

1. **One list.** `RESULTS.md` is the single numbered list of results. It is generated; nobody edits it by hand.
2. **One source.** `registry/RESULTS_LEDGER.json` holds one record per audited result: a plain statement, its kind, its evidence, the question it answers (if any), the Lean declarations with file and line, the commit that was audited, the audit outcome, its limits and a check command.
3. **Joined, not copied.** Version, repository, pin and paper path are not stored in the ledger. `scripts/build_ledger.py` joins them from `registry/PAPERS.json` and `registry/BUILD_PAPERS.json`, and reads the live mirror for upstream state. The ledger therefore follows every registry update and every live sync without anyone retyping a number.
4. **An audit is tied to a commit.** Evidence links are permalinks at the audited commit. If the archive pin moves past it, the result is shown as "re-audit pending". If the source repository moves past the pin, the result says so.
5. **Nothing is silently missing.** Every Tier I and Tier II entry appears: through its results, through a stated reason, or under "registered but not yet audited into this ledger".
6. **Numbers are permanent.** A result that is narrowed keeps its number. A result that fails is marked withdrawn and keeps its number.
7. **Wording is checked.** The generator rejects promotional wording, a "published open question answered" without a cited source and a recorded statement audit and prior-work search, a "new theorem" that is known mathematics, and a kernel-checked result without a cited declaration.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** one page a reader can check line by line; counts in `README.md` come from the ledger; the list cannot drift from the registries; a release or a pin move cannot inherit an audit it did not have.
- **Cost:** a result enters the list only after a statement audit, so the ledger can lag behind a new paper. The lag is visible, by design.
- **Limit:** the audit is an internal, AI-assisted check directed by the author. It is not peer review, and the ledger says so at the top.

## How to use

```bash
python scripts/build_ledger.py            # regenerate RESULTS.md and the README block
python scripts/build_ledger.py --check    # fail if the ledger is invalid or the outputs are stale
python scripts/build_ledger.py --check --checkouts <dir>   # also confirm each Lean declaration is at the cited line
```

`python scripts/verify_archive.py --sync` runs the first form; `python scripts/verify_archive.py` runs the second.

<!-- FILE: docs/faq.md -->

# Frequently Asked Questions (`docs/faq.md`)

### 1. Which repository is the single canonical master archive of everything `0thernes` has solved or verified?
**This repository (`0thernes/0thernes-research-archive`)** — along with its live GitHub Pages portal at [`https://0thernes.github.io/0thernes-research-archive/`](https://0thernes.github.io/0thernes-research-archive/). Specialist open-problem catalogues (`unsolved-problems-mega-atlas`, `unsolved-mathematics`, `unsolved-black-hole-problems`) remain focused domain spokes indexed inside this hub and refreshed hourly via [`.github/workflows/live-sync.yml`](../.github/workflows/live-sync.yml) (see [ADR 0002](adr/0002-canonical-hub-and-live-sync.md)).

### 2. Why are entries split into Tier I, Tier II, and Tier III?
To enforce epistemic honesty: Tier I holds standalone formalized research preprints (`PAPERS.json`), Tier II holds public software/engineering builds with embedded white papers and Pure Lean 4 invariant suites (`BUILD_PAPERS.json`), and Tier III holds architectural laws, pre-registered empirical claims (including null results), finite certificates, synthesis dossiers, and open-problem atlases (`LAWS_AND_DISCOVERIES.json`).

### 3. Have any papers in this archive retired one of the 1,900 Mega-Atlas problems?
**No (`0 / 1,900` grand Mega-Atlas problems retired).** Two questions stated as open in unreviewed arXiv preprints (`0TH-2026-006` Conjecture 7.7; `0TH-2026-009` Track 2, the Muller–Saniga Sec. 6 stacking-limit question for disjoint squares and pentagrams only) plus Jonah's Conjecture E from an unreviewed Zenodo preprint (`0TH-2026-009` Track 1: one explicit representative per vertex case in Lean; case labels and Theorem B4 of the unreviewed source outside Lean; for 0TH-2026-009 only the 12 comparator targets are six-kernel checked, and the Track 2 identification with HS(kG) is by enumeration, not Lean) are formally proved in Lean 4.35.0 within their exact published scopes; see [`registry/SOLVED_AND_ATLAS_BRIDGE.md`](../registry/SOLVED_AND_ATLAS_BRIDGE.md) and [`builds/0TH-BUILD-007_unsolved-problems-mega-atlas/0THERNES_SOLVED_AUDIT_2026-11-25.md`](../builds/0TH-BUILD-007_unsolved-problems-mega-atlas/0THERNES_SOLVED_AUDIT_2026-11-25.md).

### 4. How does the hub stay in step with the upstream repositories?
Every hour (and immediately when an upstream repository that carries `.github/workflows/notify-archive.yml` and an `ARCHIVE_SYNC_TOKEN` secret dispatches `upstream-repo-updated`; no repository had that secret on 2026-11-26), `.github/workflows/live-sync.yml` runs `scripts/live_sync.py`, updates `registry/LIVE_ECOSYSTEM_MIRROR.json/.md` and the bounded live status block in `README.md`, re-verifies SHA-256 digests and `pytest`, and redeploys GitHub Pages automatically.

### 5. How do I verify every archived PDF, link, and submodule pin locally?
Run `python3 scripts/verify_archive.py`, `sha256sum -c CHECKSUMS.sha256`, and `python3 -m pytest -v tests/`. Every hash, relative link, privacy-firewall invariant, and Git submodule pin is verified in seconds.
